title: perf(canary): enhance auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Improve performance canary auto-detection heuristics and add hysteresis and rollback guards. Reduces false positives and prevents harmful rollouts in face of transient noise.
description: This PR improves the performance canary system by enhancing automated detection of latency and throughput regressions and adding safer rollout guards. Motivation: we've seen several false-positive canary failures during noisy intervals (GC spikes, infra flaps) that triggered premature rollback or blocked rollouts. This work introduces: 1) Adaptive baseline windowing: switch between 95th-percentile windows of 5m/30m depending on traffic variance to avoid reacting to transient spikes. 2) Hysteresis and cooldown: require sustained violation across consecutive detection windows before marking a canary as failed. 3) Throughput-aware detection: separate throughput regressions from latency regressions and apply independent thresholds to avoid conflation. 4) Soft-fail and staged rollback: on first sustained detection, mark canary as "degraded" and limit traffic to a safe minimum (10%) while notifying SRE; only on repeated detections do we execute a full automated rollback. 5) Metrics tagging and tracing hooks to correlate operational noise (node restarts, GC events) and suppress alerts when correlated. Design rationale, test plan, and rollout steps are included below. NOTE: description includes implementation details, unit and integration test coverage, and a staged rollout plan to prevent large blast radius.

testing_notes: Local: added unit tests for detectors and cooldown; coverage increased for services/perf-canary to 82%
Integration: integration test replays historical traffic and injected GC noise; detection did not trigger on single transient spike
Canary e2e: staged rollout to internal org with 10% traffic for 48h, monitored stability; no rollbacks observed in pilot
rollout_plan: Step 1: Deploy to staging with feature-flag on, run full integration suite (24h)
Step 2: Enable for 10% of internal traffic, monitor SLOs and alerts for 48h
Step 3: If stable, gradually increase to 50% over 72h with slow ramp and manual checkpoints
Step 4: Enable automated rollback policy after 72h if telemetry is stable; otherwise keep soft-fail behavior
Rollback: immediate rollback script available and tested; manual override via console
